summary_paragraph: A woman with prior laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and gastrostomy tube feeds, with a history of marginal gastrojejunal ulcers, was admitted to the bariatric surgery service for one week of recurrent epigastric/left subcostal pain radiating to the back with baseline nausea. She was managed with bowel rest (initial NPO), IV pantoprazole twice daily and sucralfate, IV fluids and daily vitamin supplementation, and pain control initially with PCA; narcotics were discontinued due to nausea and dry heaving, and chronic pain service adjusted her regimen by increasing nortriptyline to 100 mg nightly and stopping Effexor with communication to her psychiatrist. Abdominal radiograph showed no free air or obstruction and moderate stool burden. Nutritional labs demonstrated iron deficiency (low iron and ferritin), and iron supplementation was adjusted to liquid iron. Symptoms improved and she tolerated a bariatric Stage 3 diet, with plans to advance as tolerated and continue cycled G-tube feeds at 60 mL/hr for 12 hours daily. She was discharged home ambulatory and stable on PPI, sucralfate, antiemetic as needed, updated pain regimen, and bariatric vitamin/iron supplementation with surgical follow-up.
problems: Gastrojejunal ulcer, unspecified as acute or chronic, without mention of hemorrhage or perforation, without mention of obstruction
